answer: The cipher detector writes to whisper, and relic shows every merge. A farm scripting its whole farm fires them together, which means the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 77 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. Submissions that land within 61 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. That is 29 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
